findings.title: Snapshot --files-from before the transfer can overwrite it
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/run_log.rs:173 — begin_record now runs concurrently with the transfer, but job_spec still reads --files-from from disk at line 733. Reproduced with the unmodified binary by holding the machine-id read until a copy overwrote its destination-side list: the transfer copied a.txt and list.txt, but --export recorded files_from as ["b.txt"], the replacement list's contents.
findings.predicted_failure: Without --save, a transfer that overwrites its --files-from file before deferred initialization reaches job_spec silently stores a different job. Running the exported job subsequently selects b.txt instead of the original a.txt and list.txt.
findings.better_approach: Capture the list contents before transfer dispatch, preferably sharing the parsed selection with the transfer, and defer only persistence of that captured specification.

findings.title: Preserve the command's start timestamp across deferred initialization
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/run_log.rs:173 — deferred begin_record calls RunRecord::starting at line 596, which assigns started_ms from the current time. With a delayed machine-id read, the unmodified binary exported a record whose started_ms was 1,206 ms after the copied file was already present; its log correctly retained the earlier run-start timestamp.
findings.predicted_failure: Slow initialization records the worker's initialization time as the command's start. jobs list displays incorrect start times and can reorder overlapping commands; exported timestamps can imply that a completed transfer began after its file operations.
findings.better_approach: Capture the start timestamp in CommandRun::start and pass it to the background record initializer.
